cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Bring Back Everything
cards.instruction: Return early details in altered forms until the scene feels like it has been building toward one unavoidable consequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put the cake on that spare chair. I'll keep the table clear until everyone has sat down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That leaves one guest without a seat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give them the piano stool. The pianist can stand for the birthday song; I'll tell him when to start.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He needs both hands to play, and the guest has put the cake on his lap so he can use the chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the pianist can have his stool back. Bring the chair to the table and put the cake on it; I'll cut it now. We've seated everyone except the thing I was saving for later.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 directs cake on chair and A3 seating substitution, but A5 orders cake back on occupied chair while claiming everyone seated; combined-card outcome fails physical coherence.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2 missing seat; B4 guest solves by holding cake; A5 undoes that solution by returning cake to chair and ignoring displacement.

relationship.evidence: B2 seat concern and B4 guest solution plausible, but B4 both-hands claim is irrelevant to standing playing and pronouns blur guest/pianist.

heightening.evidence: A5 early serving could resolve chain but instead returns to original occupancy problem while claiming resolution.

specificity.evidence: A5 chair still needed by guest; cake cannot occupy it while guest remains seated unless new arrangement explained.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 thing saving for later is clear metaphor but cannot rescue contradictory staging.
